title: Linguine with plaice, peas and lemon

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain staple: peas, plaice, dried pasta, butter, crème fraîche, spring onions, garlic, lemon and dill.

supermarket.reason: Plaice fillets, peas in the pod in June, linguine and crème fraîche are all everyday mainstream supermarket items.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large pan and a frying pan, and the techniques are simple boiling and pan-frying.

works.reason: 350g pasta, 400g plaice and about 240g podded peas with 200ml crème fraîche loosened with pasta water makes a balanced, well-sauced dinner for four, and the timings are sound.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers podding 600g of peas, slicing the onions and garlic and frying the fish, and 12 minutes matches the pasta boiling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, dill, salt and pepper, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted apart from water is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A light lemony pasta with freshly podded peas suits late June, and the peas are a named main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are plain, brief British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a proper family dinner with fish protein, a good share of vegetables and pasta.
